# HRP Rule 2 - Play a persistent, consistent character You are free to create and play whatever characters you like, and to portray them however you want. This standard asks only that a character stays believable while you are playing them. It is not a demand that you commit to one fixed personality forever.
- You are welcome to play many different characters, and to reinvent, change, or retire a character whenever you like. - How you play a character, their personality, quirks, mood, and outlook, is entirely up to you and may change over time. - Within a single round, keep your character believable and coherent. Do not flip your personality mid-shift purely for a mechanical edge with no in-character reason. - Carrying the same character across rounds and developing them over time is encouraged, but never required. - Your character's identity is yours to shape. Specific round events still do not carry over; acting on what happened in a previous round is metagaming and is covered by the Metashield.
Part of that freedom is getting into trouble. You can start a fight in the hallways if that is who your character is, but be ready to face the consequences in character and to follow [textlink="high-roleplay escalation" link="RuleH3"]. If you overdo it or ignore reasonable escalation, expect a message from the admins via ahelp.
